facts.text: Park Rapids was founded in 1890 beside the Fish Hook River rapids, where prairie meets pine forest, becoming a key supply depot for farmers and lumber.
After being platted, Park Rapids residents founded a Ladies Library that opened a free public library in the fire station, later relocating it to a former bank in 1994.
In 2022, the Anishinaabe nonprofit Akiing purchased the former library building and renamed it the Giiwedinong Treaty Rights and Culture Museum, part of a Land Back effort.
The land that is now Park Rapids was originally inhabited by Ojibwe people, who still maintain a significant presence in the region.
Park Rapids sits along the Fish Hook River and is surrounded by three lakes—Fish Hook, Long, and Potato—providing ample fishing opportunities.
